hook_text: Your phone, your rice, your petrol: almost none of it was made in South Africa. So what do we send the other way?
clip_script: No country has everything. South Africa has platinum, gold, coal, iron ore and good land for oranges and grapes. But very little oil. So we sell what we have and buy what we lack. Exports go out: platinum, coal, cars, citrus. Imports come in: oil, phones, machines, medicines. Exports minus imports: the balance of trade. And none of it moves without transport. Most of the world's trade by weight crosses the sea, packed into steel containers that cranes swing from ship to train to truck. Durban handles more of them than any other port in the country. Trade and transport: you cannot have one without the other.
visual_style: A whiteboard world map with arrows of exports leaving South Africa and imports arriving, a container being lifted from ship to train, and a simple balance scale for exports and imports.
pacing: Quick contrasts, steady explanation of the balance of trade.
